name: Quantum Computing
description: Qubits, gates and circuits, the main quantum algorithms, noise and error correction, and programming real devices.

nodes.name: Complex linear algebra
nodes.desc: Complex vectors, inner products and unitary and Hermitian matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute with complex vectors and matrices and recognise unitary and Hermitian matrices used in quantum mechanics.

nodes.name: Dirac notation
nodes.desc: Kets, bras, inner and outer products.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read and write quantum states and operators in Dirac notation using kets, bras and their products.

nodes.name: Tensor products
nodes.desc: Combining systems with tensor products of vectors and matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe multi-qubit systems with tensor products of vectors and matrices.

nodes.name: Measurement
nodes.desc: Amplitudes, the Born rule and measurement in different bases.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute measurement outcome probabilities with the Born rule and measure states in different bases.

nodes.name: Qubits & Bloch sphere
nodes.desc: Single-qubit states, superposition and the Bloch sphere picture.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent single-qubit states as superpositions and visualise them as points on the Bloch sphere.

nodes.name: Single-qubit gates
nodes.desc: Pauli, Hadamard and phase gates as rotations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply Pauli, Hadamard and phase gates to qubits and interpret them as rotations of the Bloch sphere.
topics: Pauli X, Y and Z gates
Rotation gates Rx, Ry and Rz

nodes.name: Multi-qubit gates
nodes.desc: CNOT, controlled gates and multi-qubit states.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply CNOT and other controlled gates to multi-qubit states and compute the resulting states.

nodes.name: Entanglement
nodes.desc: Bell states, teleportation and superdense coding.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prepare Bell states and explain how entanglement enables quantum teleportation and superdense coding.

nodes.name: Quantum circuits
nodes.desc: Circuit model, reversibility and universal gate sets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build and read quantum circuits and explain reversibility and universal gate sets.

nodes.name: Deutsch-Jozsa
nodes.desc: Oracles, phase kickback and the first quantum speed-ups.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how oracles and phase kickback give the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm an exponential query advantage.

nodes.name: Quantum Fourier
nodes.desc: The quantum Fourier transform and its circuit.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define the quantum Fourier transform and build its circuit from Hadamard and controlled phase gates.
topics: Gate count compared with the FFT

nodes.name: Phase estimation
nodes.desc: Estimating eigenphases of unitaries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate the eigenphase of a unitary with quantum phase estimation and analyse its precision.

nodes.name: Shor's algorithm
nodes.desc: Factoring via period finding and its impact on RSA.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how Shor's algorithm reduces factoring to period finding and why it threatens RSA.
topics: Reduction from factoring to order finding
Impact on RSA and resource estimates

nodes.name: Grover's search
nodes.desc: Amplitude amplification and the quadratic speed-up for search.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run Grover's search with amplitude amplification and compute the optimal number of iterations.

nodes.name: Noise & decoherence
nodes.desc: Density matrices, quantum channels and decoherence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe noisy quantum states with density matrices and model decoherence with quantum channels.

nodes.name: Error correction
nodes.desc: Bit-flip and phase-flip codes, the Shor code and stabilisers.
nodes.summary: You will understand how quantum error-correcting codes detect and fix errors without measuring the encoded information.

nodes.name: Quantum hardware
nodes.desc: Superconducting, trapped-ion and photonic qubits and their trade-offs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare superconducting, trapped-ion and photonic qubit technologies by fidelity, connectivity and scalability.

nodes.name: Variational algorithms
nodes.desc: VQE and QAOA as hybrid quantum-classical methods.
nodes.summary: You will understand how VQE and QAOA combine parameterised quantum circuits with classical optimisers.

nodes.name: Quantum cryptography
nodes.desc: BB84 key distribution and post-quantum cryptography.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how BB84 detects eavesdroppers and why post-quantum cryptography is needed against quantum attacks.

nodes.name: Quantum programming
nodes.desc: Writing and simulating circuits with a quantum SDK and running on hardware.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write, simulate and run quantum circuits with a quantum SDK on simulators and real hardware.
topics: Building circuits with an SDK like Qiskit

nodes.name: Algorithm simulator
nodes.desc: Implement Grover and a small Shor instance and compare simulator and device results.
nodes.summary: You will implement Grover's search and a small Shor instance and compare results from simulators and real quantum devices.
